title: Sodom and the Son of Promise, part 5 of 6: the death of Sarah and the cave of Machpelah
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The age of the patriarchs in the ancient Near East, about four thousand years ago: people dressed in simple garments of wool or linen, undyed or dyed in earth colours, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

ABRAHAM.name: Abraham
ABRAHAM.desc: Abraham, a tall, upright old man who looks about eighty and is still strong, with warm brown, deeply weathered and lined skin, thick wavy white hair reaching his collar, a full white beard, white eyebrows, a strong straight nose and steady, thoughtful dark eyes, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool with a brown leather belt and a deep russet-red wool mantle draped over his left shoulder, and simple leather sandals

SARAH.name: Sarah
SARAH.desc: Sarah, a graceful, dignified old woman who looks about seventy and is still beautiful, with warm brown skin finely lined at the eyes and mouth, large dark eyes, high cheekbones and long wavy silver-grey hair, her hair mostly covered by a long indigo-blue wool head shawl that falls over her shoulders, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved dress of undyed cream wool with a woven belt of red and blue, and simple leather sandals

EPHRON.name: Ephron
EPHRON.desc: Ephron the Hittite, a prosperous landowner of about fifty, stocky and broad-shouldered, with light olive-brown skin, a round, full face with heavy-lidded dark eyes and a broad nose, thick black hair to his shoulders held by a plain narrow bronze band around his head, and a short, squared black beard with a patch of grey at the chin, wearing a knee-length short-sleeved tunic of fine ochre-yellow wool with a woven border of red and blue at the hem, a wide dark-red cloth sash, one heavy plain bronze armlet on his right upper arm, and leather sandals

blocks.ONE: Exactly one person in the picture, no one else
blocks.HANDS: Only hands and forearms are in the frame, no faces
blocks.EMPTY: A pure landscape with no human being in it: not one person, figure or silhouette anywhere, near or far
blocks.TENT: a low, wide tent of black goat-hair cloth stretched over wooden poles and held by ropes and wooden pegs
blocks.SERVANTS: herdsmen and serving women in knee-length tunics and ankle-length dresses of rough wool in undyed cream, brown and grey, the women with plain head shawls
blocks.CANAAN: the hill country of Canaan: rolling limestone hills with grey rock ledges, spring grass, wild flowers, scattered olive trees and thickets of evergreen oak
blocks.NOHALO: No halo, no rays and no glow around any person
blocks.HEBRON: the town of Hebron: a small walled Canaanite town of pale stone and mud brick with flat roofs, on a hillside among olive groves and vineyards; no domes, no arches, no columns, no towers with pointed roofs
blocks.GATE: the open square just inside the gate of the town: a wide gateway of big pale stone blocks roofed with heavy timber beams, its thick wooden doors standing open to the sunlit hills outside, and low stone benches along the walls where the men of the town sit; no arches, no columns, no carvings, no statues, no writing
blocks.HITTITES: the Hittites of the town, the sons of Heth: bearded townsmen with black or iron-grey hair to their shoulders held by cloth headbands, in knee-length wrapped wool kilts and tunics of brown, grey, dull green and cream with red and blue woven borders, some with a mantle over one shoulder; only grown men, all unarmed: no helmets, no armour, no spears, no swords; none of them has white hair and none wears a red mantle or a yellow tunic
blocks.GATEBG: The background is only the stone gateway, its benches and the townsmen: no tents, no animals, no market stalls, no banners
blocks.SHROUD: the body of his wife lies on a low bed of woven rugs, wrapped from head to foot in plain undyed cream linen with a long indigo-blue wool shawl laid lengthwise over it, so that it is only a still, covered shape: no face, no hands, no hair and no skin are seen
blocks.INTENT: inside a tent of black goat-hair cloth by day, dim and quiet, with wooden poles, woven rugs on the ground and soft grey daylight falling in through the open door flap; indoors: no animals, no sky
blocks.FIELD: Ephron's field at Machpelah: a sloping field of spring grass and young green barley edged by a low boundary wall of piled field stones, with old olive trees, oaks and terebinths standing in it and along its edges, among limestone hills
blocks.CAVE: the cave of Machpelah: the low, dark mouth of a natural cave, about as high as a man, opening in a ledge of grey limestone at the far end of a field and half shaded by an old oak; a natural opening in the living rock, with no masonry, no doorway, no steps, no carving and no building
blocks.SILVER: pieces of silver: small rough-cut lumps, broken rings and short bent rods of dull white silver, not coins; there are no round stamped coins anywhere
blocks.SCALE: a small hand-held balance scale: a thin straight wooden beam hanging level from a cord held in one hand, with a shallow round bronze pan hanging from each end of the beam on three threads
blocks.WEIGHTS: small weights of dark polished stone, smooth and dome-shaped like little loaves, with nothing written or carved on them
blocks.BIER: a simple bier made of two long wooden poles with rope webbing between them, on which lies a still shape wrapped from head to foot in plain undyed cream linen with a long indigo-blue wool shawl laid lengthwise over it: no face, no hands and no skin are seen
blocks.NOTENTS: No tents, no walls, no buildings and no animals anywhere
blocks.ONLYA: He is the only white-haired man and the only one with a red mantle
blocks.ONLYE: Ephron is the only man in a yellow tunic

segs.text: Now Sarah lived to be 127 years old.
She died in Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went out to mourn and to weep for her.
Then Abraham got up from beside his dead wife and said to the Hittites,
I am a foreigner and an outsider among you. Give me a burial site among you so that I can bury my dead.
The Hittites replied to Abraham,
Listen to us, sir. You are God’s chosen one among us. Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs. None of us will withhold his tomb for burying your dead.
Then Abraham rose and bowed down before the people of the land, the Hittites.
If you are willing for me to bury my dead,
he said to them,
listen to me, and approach Ephron son of Zohar on my behalf
to sell me the cave of Machpelah that belongs to him; it is at the end of his field. Let him sell it to me in your presence for full price, so that I may have a burial site.
Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth. So in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city, Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham,
No, my lord. Listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. I give it to you in the presence of my people. Bury your dead.
Again Abraham bowed down before the people of the land
and said to Ephron in their presence,
If you will please listen to me, I will pay you the price of the field. Accept it from me, so that I may bury my dead there.
Ephron answered Abraham,
Listen to me, my lord. The land is worth four hundred shekels of silver, but what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.
Abraham agreed to Ephron’s terms and weighed out for him the price he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver, according to the standard of the merchants.
So Ephron’s field at Machpelah near Mamre, the cave that was in it, and all the trees within the boundaries of the field were deeded over
to Abraham’s possession in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city.
After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.
So the field and its cave were deeded by the Hittites to Abraham as a burial site.

{ABRAHAM}, walks alone up a stony path toward the open gate of {HEBRON}, seen from behind and a little to one side, small against the pale town wall, a plain wooden staff in his hand, in clear morning light. A few townsmen sit in the shadow of the distant gateway. No tents, no animals. Wide view.

I am a foreigner and an outsider among you: medium close view of {ABRAHAM}, standing in the shade of a gateway of big pale stone blocks, speaking humbly with one hand laid flat on his chest, his eyes red from weeping. Behind him only the pale stone wall and the open gate with sunlit hills beyond. {ONE}. {NOHALO}. No tents, no animals. Medium close view.

The men of the town listen: six of {HITTITES}, sit side by side on a low stone bench against a wall of big pale stone blocks, in shade, all looking toward the left at someone outside the picture, grave and attentive; one leans forward with his elbows on his knees, one strokes his beard. Exactly six men. {GATEBG}. Medium view.

The Hittites replied to Abraham: in {GATE}, seen from behind the right shoulder of {ABRAHAM}, who stands in the left foreground with his back to us. Facing him, a grey-bearded elder of {HITTITES}, has risen from the stone bench and stretches one open hand toward the old man in respect, while the other townsmen sit around him. {ONLYA}. {GATEBG}. Medium wide view.

You are God's chosen one among us: close view of three of {HITTITES}, in the shade of a stone gateway, looking with open respect toward someone outside the picture on the left; the grey-bearded man in the middle is speaking, his open palm turned upward. The finest of our tombs: a quiet limestone slope outside a town wall in morning light, with a row of four burial caves cut into the rock, each low dark mouth closed by a large rough boulder, and old olive trees growing between them. None of us will withhold his tomb: in {GATE}, {ABRAHAM}, stands in the middle, seen from the front, his head a little bowed. Around him in a half circle stand eight of {HITTITES}, each holding one open hand out toward him in offering. {ONLYA}. {GATEBG}. Medium wide view.

In the presence of all who had come to the gate of his city: {GATE}, crowded with about twenty of {HITTITES}, seated on the benches and standing along the walls. No, my lord. Listen to me: medium close view of {EPHRON}, standing in the shade of a stone gateway, speaking grandly toward the left with a generous smile, his right arm swept wide and his left hand on his chest. Behind him townsmen in brown and grey tunics look on. {ONLYE}. {GATEBG}. Medium close view.

Exactly three men. {ONLYA}. {NOTENTS}. Medium wide view.

Medium wide view.

card_title: A Grave in the Promised Land
card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 23:1–20, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 23:1-20 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, A Abraham (same voice as in earlier units), H the Hittites speaking together (23:6, one voice), E Ephron (23:11, 23:15). The local BSB snapshot was read verse by verse for this chapter; no slips found.
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. REF = character reference sheet (not used in the film, no clip). Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

Faces: Abraham is painted from refs/REF-ABRAHAM.jpg (key ABRAHAM, description copied word for word from s02e01e). He is 137 here (Sarah was ten years younger, 17:17), but the text says nothing of how he looked, so the sheet made for ninety-nine is kept unchanged (I). Sarah appears alive only in A1, from refs/REF-SARAH.jpg (key SARAH, copied word for word), as a picture of her last years for 23:1; how she looked at 127 is I.

New in this unit: refs/REF-EPHRON.jpg (key EPHRON), Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite. His looks, age and dress are I: a prosperous landowner of about fifty in an ochre-yellow tunic with a bronze headband, so that he can be told apart from the other townsmen in every picture. He appears again only by name (25:9, 49:29-30, 50:13).

The Hittites (sons of Heth): who these people of Hebron were, and how they relate to the Hittites of Anatolia, is disputed. They are painted as townsmen of Canaan like those of s02e01a (block HITTITES, based on its CANAANITES block), with nothing Anatolian and no writing, so the picture decides nothing. They are unarmed men at their town gate (23:10, 23:18).
Sarah's body is never shown: from B2 on it is a shape wrapped in cream linen under her indigo-blue shawl (blocks SHROUD and BIER; the wrapping and the shawl are I). No face, hands or skin.

23:2 'Abraham went out to mourn': he is painted walking to the tent where she lies (B3). Where he came from is not shown: 22:19 has him living at Beersheba and the question whether he was away when she died is left open. The tent stands under an oak near Hebron (I, from 13:18, 18:1 and 23:17 'near Mamre'). Isaac and Ishmael are not named in this chapter and are not shown; the bearers at the burial are unnamed men of the household (I).

23:7 and 23:12 'bowed down': painted both times as a very deep bow from the waist with the head lowered, from two different sides (F1, K1); the exact posture (a bow or full prostration) is I. The Hittites never bow to him.

23:6 'the finest of our tombs' (E3): closed burial caves in a rock slope outside the wall (I). 23:9, 23:17 the cave of Machpelah: a natural cave mouth in a rock ledge at the end of a field with trees (T: cave, end of the field, trees, boundaries; its shape is I). Nothing of the later building over the traditional site is shown.

23:16 the silver: weighed, not counted (T). Painted as rough pieces, rings and rods of silver on a hand balance against plain stone weights (I, from the period: there were no coins). 'Four hundred shekels' is spoken as written and the amount is not pictured as a count; whether the price was fair or high is not decided (Ephron smiles and shrugs in M1 and M2, which is D).

23:17-18, 23:20 'deeded': the BSB word is kept in the narration, but no tablet, scroll or writing is shown: the transfer is pictured as the text describes it, by spoken words, the weighed silver and the townsmen as witnesses at the gate (O4, the raised hands are D).

23:19 the burial: a bier carried across the field into the cave (P1, P2), the body laid on a rock ledge (P3), Abraham's hand on the shawl (P4, I), and a boulder set in the cave mouth (P5, I, as in E3). No prayer or rite is shown because the text names none. God does not speak or appear in this chapter and is not pictured.

Style line: 'tents of black goat hair' is left out of this unit's style (lesson of s02e01a: it puts tents and goats into every background); tents are named only in the pictures that have one (A1, B2-B5, C1).
